AU.hint: Blue with the Union Jack, a big seven-pointed star, and five white stars. New Zealand has four red stars.
AU.funFact: Australia is the only country that is also a whole continent.

NZ.hint: Blue with the Union Jack and four red stars outlined in white (the Southern Cross).
NZ.funFact: New Zealand was the first country to give women the vote, in 1893.

FJ.hint: Light blue with the Union Jack and a shield showing a lion, sugarcane, a coconut palm, bananas and a dove.
FJ.funFact: Fiji has about 330 islands, and around 110 of them are inhabited.

PG.hint: Split diagonally: red with a gold bird-of-paradise, and black with five white stars.
PG.funFact: More than 800 languages are spoken in Papua New Guinea, more than in any other country.

SB.hint: A thin yellow diagonal stripe between blue and green, with five white stars in the top-left.
SB.funFact: Guadalcanal, its largest island, saw some of the fiercest battles of World War II.

VU.hint: Red and green halves split by a black-edged yellow sideways 'Y', with a curled boar's tusk on black.
VU.funFact: Bungee jumping was inspired by Vanuatu's 'land diving' ritual on Pentecost Island.

FM.hint: Light blue with four white stars in a diamond, one for each state.
FM.funFact: On Yap island, giant stone discs called Rai stones, some 4 m wide, were used as money.

KI.hint: Red top with a golden frigatebird over a rising sun, and blue and white waves at the bottom.
KI.funFact: Kiribati is the only country that lies in all four hemispheres.

MH.hint: Blue with two diagonal stripes (orange and white) and a large 24-pointed white star.
MH.funFact: Bikini Atoll, where the USA tested nuclear bombs, is in the Marshall Islands.

NR.hint: Blue with a thin yellow line (the equator) and a white 12-pointed star below it.
NR.funFact: Nauru is the world's smallest island country and has no official capital.

PW.hint: Light blue with a yellow circle (the moon) set slightly off-centre.
PW.funFact: Palau created the world's first shark sanctuary in 2009.

WS.hint: Red with a blue top-left corner holding five white stars (the Southern Cross).
WS.funFact: In 2011 Samoa skipped 30 December entirely to move to the other side of the International Date Line.

TO.hint: Red with a white top-left square holding a red cross.
TO.funFact: Tonga's constitution says the flag can never be changed.

TV.hint: Light blue with the Union Jack and nine yellow stars arranged like its islands.
TV.funFact: Tuvalu earns millions by leasing out its '.tv' internet domain.
